summary.car: Formula Ultimate Hybrid Gen2 - High Downforce

findings.title: T4: you lose 0.38 s per lap on average vs your best pass
findings.detail: you usually brake 18 m earlier than on your fastest pass; your fastest pass was 5.2 km/h slower at the apex but got out better.

findings.title: T9: 48 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T7: 34 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T10: 23 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T4: 22 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T4: brake peak only 55%
findings.detail: For a 101 km/h speed drop you should hit the brake much harder at first (80-100%), then bleed it off. Soft initial braking forces an early brake point.

findings.title: T5: 16 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T3: ABS active 49% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T6: ABS active 44% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T7: ABS active 36% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T9: ABS active 37% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T10: ABS active 64% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

setup.title: No consistent balance problem detected
setup.detail: Handling looks reasonably neutral from the data. Focus on driving technique first.

setup.title: Rear wheels locking
setup.detail: Move brake bias 1-2% forward (telemetry reads 44%; check the garage value). Rear lockups make the car unstable into corners.

setup.title: Front ride height under 1 cm for 11.1% of the time at speed
setup.detail: The car is probably touching the ground. Low-downforce cars should not do this; for high-downforce cars some is normal. If the car feels nervous over bumps, kerbs or in fast corners, raise ride height a few mm or stiffen springs/bump stops on that axle.

setup.title: Rear ride height under 1 cm for 5.7% of the time at speed
setup.detail: The car is probably touching the ground. Low-downforce cars should not do this; for high-downforce cars some is normal. If the car feels nervous over bumps, kerbs or in fast corners, raise ride height a few mm or stiffen springs/bump stops on that axle.

setup.title: Rears running 32.2°C hotter
setup.detail: Rears are overworked: wheelspin or oversteer. Smoother throttle and the exit-oversteer fixes help.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 3 of 8 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T3, T6, T9. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T2, T3, T4, T5, T7, T9, T10)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: Flat out through the fast corners (T1, T8)
pros.detail: You trust the car through the quick sections without lifting. Keep doing that.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 8 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: 50.9% of the lap at full throttle
pros.detail: Strong commitment on the straights and exits for this track.

pros.title: Consistent through T1, T8
pros.detail: Your section times there barely change from pass to pass, so you have found a repeatable approach.

cons.title: Coasting: 22.5% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 143 m per lap in T4, T5, T7, T9, T10. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Braking into ABS in 5 corners
cons.detail: In T3, T6, T7, T9, T10 ABS is active for 64% of the zone at worst. ABS is a safety net; leaning on it lengthens your stops and hides where the real limit is.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 7 corners
cons.detail: T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T9, T10. Your rear tyres run 32°C hotter than the fronts, which is a symptom. Spinning wheels don't accelerate the car; they just cook the tyres.

cons.title: Throttle on-off-on at the apex (T4)
cons.detail: You pick up the throttle, lift, then reapply. That unsettles the car and usually means you went to the throttle too hard or too early.

cons.title: Too gentle at the start of braking (T4)
cons.detail: Peak pressure only 55%. A soft start forces you to brake earlier and longer.

cons.title: Wheels locking (T5, T10)
cons.detail: Locked wheels don't steer and flat-spot the tyre.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T6, T4, T3, T10, T2, T9
cons.detail: T6: 0.56 s between your average and best pass; T4: 0.38 s between your average and best pass; T3: 0.28 s between your average and best pass; T10: 0.26 s between your average and best pass; T2: 0.23 s between your average and best pass; T9: 0.18 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T9, T7.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit 90-100% immediately at high speed, then progressively release as the car slows. A formula car loses downforce as it slows, so the same pedal pressure that was fine at 280 km/h locks the wheels at 120 km/h.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Pick fixed reference points
improve.how: For T6, T4, T3: choose one brake marker (a board, a shadow, a kerb start) and one turn-in point, and use them every lap. Move the brake marker 5 m later only when you hit the apex 3 laps in a row.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Stabbing the throttle and lifting again
stopDoing.detail: Pick it up once, gently, and only ever add more.

stopDoing.title: Braking gently at the start of a big stop
stopDoing.detail: Brake hardest at the beginning, not the end.

stopDoing.title: Keeping full brake pressure as speed drops
stopDoing.detail: Downforce falls as you slow; release pressure progressively.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (22.5% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Cold formula tyres lock and spin easily. Check them on the out-lap and after a slide, on straights only.
Formula cars expect you to adjust these during a lap. Only look at them on straights.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Steering lock: formula cars use much less rotation than road or GT cars (roughly 360-540°). Let AMS2 set the soft lock for the car, and keep the in-game rotation matched to Pit House so the on-screen wheel turns exactly as far as yours.

Force feedback: high-downforce cars produce big forces in fast corners, so clipping is likely on a 5.5 Nm R5. Turn on AMS2's FFB HUD meter and lower in-game gain until the bar only touches the top briefly.
Keep damping and inertia low in Pit House (as in your R5-AMS2-Claude preset). Formula steering should feel quick and light at low speed.
Learn with brake bias slightly rearward of where it locks the fronts, and ABS/TC on if the car allows it; turn them off later.
